outliers.title: Every aircraft carrier lands its jets on a crooked runway #navy #aviation #aircraftcarrier
outliers.description: Every modern aircraft carrier lands its jets on a strip angled about nine degrees off the bow. On the old straight decks, a jet that missed the arresting wires was caught by a steel barrier and a net, because the other planes were parked at the front. Jets came in heavier and faster, and on 16 September 1951 a damaged jet landing on USS Essex bounced over the barriers into the parked planes; seven men died. outliers.title: The biggest plane ever to land on an aircraft carrier did it with no hook
outliers.description:
In October and November 1963, the U.S. Navy tested a KC-130F Hercules on loan from the Marines aboard the carrier USS Forrestal. Lt. James H. Flatley III made 29 touch-and-go landings, 21 unarrested full-stop landings and 21 unassisted takeoffs. At about 85,000 pounds, it stopped in roughly 267 feet. It's still the largest and heaviest aircraft to land on a carrier, but the Navy decided routine use was too risky.
